constraints: One to sixteen already-resident immutable blobs, each zero to 65536 bytes; no input streaming or joined aggregate copy.
Authenticate the immutable envelope/policy before evidence hashing; require complete digest-set equality and preserve every signed outcome.
Metadata-only return, no content interpretation, storage, transport, qualification or authority. No defined hardware, deadline, RSS or throughput target.
alternatives: CPython exact bytes/tuple admission and native hashlib.
Rust owned or safely borrowed immutable input with sha2.
C#/F# SHA256.HashData over caller-owned stable buffers.
Node JavaScript/TypeScript crypto with explicit ownership for mutable buffers.
rationale: KEEP the immutable snapshot plus native hash implementation: exact-type admission prevents mutable backing stores from changing between validation, authentication and hashing; bounded per-blob hashing avoids joining content.

Rust borrowing, .NET spans and BEAM binary handling are credible alternatives; an FFI boundary does not inherently require copying. No measured or specified deployment advantage establishes a winning migration.

Ten focused binding methods pass, including maximum input, empty content, all-before-hash rejection, signed negative outcomes and backend failure. Weakening exact set equality causes two expected assertion failures.
Candidate choice is based on data ownership, complete set semantics and documented hash APIs, not installed tools, incumbent language, familiarity or rewrite cost.
limits: One MiB bounds evidence input content, not interpreter/native memory or RSS. Returned digests can correlate guessable content; they are not anonymization or encryption.
Frozen result metadata is not an unforgeable token; the caller must reverify at use and handle input/result privacy. No secure erasure is promised.
